findings: SOLR-18616 and its comments, parent SOLR-18147 and its comments, and linked SOLR-17855 were read through JIRA. Parent concerns a new monitoring dashboard, alerts and push support; it does not prescribe a Jetty implementation. Jan's ticket comment proposes a Jetty StatisticsHandler pull bridge and acknowledges lack of per-method counts. Hoss identifies initialization and SolrMetricManager registration as an obstacle.

The pre-removal parent of cee53df8e0a used Dropwizard 4.2.26 and Jetty 12.0.19. solr/server/etc/jetty.xml creates InstrumentedQueuedThreadPool with SharedMetricRegistries.getOrCreate('solr.jetty'); the InstrumentedEE10Handler wraps DefaultHandler as the second member after InetAccessHandler/ContextHandlerCollection in Handler.Sequence. The 9.x branch uses Jetty 10 variants, a HandlerCollection and the same registry. This placement means old Jetty 12 handler coverage should not be assumed to be all traffic; verify actual chain behavior with tests.

Dropwizard 4.2.26 AbstractInstrumentedHandler registers requests and dispatches timers, active-requests, active-dispatches and active-suspended counters, async-dispatches and async-timeouts meters, response-class 1xx through 5xx meters, HTTP method timers for GET POST HEAD PUT DELETE OPTIONS TRACE CONNECT MOVE and other, and 4xx/5xx one-, five- and fifteen-minute rate-ratio gauges. Default response level is coarse, not per exact status. Timers contain counts and duration distributions; meter rates and exponentially weighted ratios are not automatically identical to OTel histograms or PromQL rates. Names are Dropwizard suffixes; exact exported Prometheus mapping and Jetty 10 differences remain to be checked.

InstrumentedQueuedThreadPool 4.2.26 registers size, jobs, jobs-queue-utilization, utilization = utilized/(threads - leased), and utilization-max = getUtilizationRate(). Its own getter semantics and denominator matter: pool jobs and utilized threads do not equal HTTP requests in flight.

Pinned main catalog and server lockfile list Jetty 12.1.14, OTel API/SDK 1.65.0, Prometheus exporter 1.65.0-alpha and runtime telemetry 2.31.1-alpha, but no OTel Jetty server handler or servlet instrumentation artifact. Jetty server/util are shipped. Main jetty.xml configures the ordinary thread pool and RewriteHandler -> Handler.Sequence -> InetAccessHandler -> ContextHandlerCollection; the sequence has no explicit DefaultHandler. It statically creates the webapp and exposes Jetty classes to it via parent classloader rules. JettySolrRunner builds QueuedThreadPool and its own handler chain at lines 207 and 397-407; integration tests need both test runner and actual distribution configuration.

CoreContainer constructs SolrMetricManager at CoreContainer.java:408. SolrMetricManager owns named MeterProviders and readers, initializes runtime JVM metrics when enabled, and MetricsHandler collects its registered readers (MetricsHandler.java:138-146). CoreContainerProvider initializes from the servlet context. A separately initialized global OTel agent is not automatically collected by this endpoint. Locating the running Jetty server and handler safely across webapp/server classloaders and lifecycle is not yet established.

Jetty 12.1.14 StatisticsHandler extends EventsHandler and exposes request/handle totals, current and max concurrency, timing aggregates, response classes, failures and bytes, but not method breakdown, async timeout/dispatch, or equivalent histogram distributions. It resets at start, and getRequestTotal, getHandleTotal, response class and failure getters return int cast from long adders/statistics: wraparound is a material risk for cumulative OTel counters on long-lived busy nodes. A proposed scrape bridge must not present these as robust unbounded monotonic counters without addressing overflow/reset. It cannot by itself restore the full inventory. Jetty's QueuedThreadPool supplies a direct candidate source for pool gauges. The existing OTel runtime instrumentation is JVM-focused; the OTel project's Jetty server support is agent instrumentation, not a currently shipped standalone server handler. No claim is made that every external alternative has been exhausted.

At pinned branch_9x, versions.lock names Jetty 10.0.26 and Dropwizard metrics-jetty10 4.2.40. Its handler has the same metric suffix inventory as the above 12 variant. Its pool utilization is (threads-idle)/threads and utilization-max is (threads-idle)/maxThreads, unlike the Jetty 12 implementation's utilized and leased accounting; this is a semantic change, not a drop-in comparable ratio.

Tentative design, not authorization: insert a server-scope EventsHandler outside RewriteHandler/sequence so valid Solr, invalid collection and outside-context requests reach it, with fixed bounded method labels including OTHER, completion status-class labels, active requests, and duration histogram; use actual completion/failure semantics, avoid counting raw paths, and account for unhandled responses and asynchronous callbacks once. Bridge to a SolrMetricManager-owned provider only after initialization and remove callbacks on shutdown/reload. Register direct thread-pool current/max/idle/leased/utilized/queue gauges with clear semantics. The exact cross-classloader handoff, early requests, server shutdown, status on unhandled requests and handler insertion order need a proof before choosing a concrete implementation.

Likely touch points: solr/server/etc/jetty.xml and perhaps server packaging for any server-loaded custom handler, a Jetty-to-Solr bridge near CoreContainerProvider/SolrMetricManager, JettySolrRunner, integration tests, metrics documentation and a changelog/unreleased YAML entry with author Nick Shanin. Tests should scrape real endpoint before/after GET and abnormal PUT for valid and invalid paths both inside and outside context; check status/method and no duplicate counts, async completion and failure, concurrent requests and pool limits, startup/shutdown/disabled metrics and absent or custom Jetty environments; test production distribution config separately from JettySolrRunner. Linux gate required; no implementation or Gradle run performed.

Rough size is medium-to-large, particularly lifecycle/classloading and distribution proof; no estimate of exact time is justified before a spike. Decisions: headline visibility versus full historical metric parity, whether per-method counts are required in first slice, naming and OTel conventions, handling startup and non-Jetty embedding, counter overflow, distributions versus rates and compatibility expectations. ConnectionStatistics is extra scope, not needed to establish the two stated impacts.
remaining: Inspect thread replies directly (archive page could not be opened, search exposed Hoss's two messages); inspect all ticket links as appropriate; validate full classloader and bridge design, actual HTTP completion handling and exact legacy Prometheus export naming. This is not a completed scope deliverable.
